characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Thermo Fisher Scientific, Talos F200X G2
characterization_methods.key_findings: SAED shows the presence of (Ti, V)C carbides and κ-carbides; a few discrete dark faceted particles are sparsely distributed in the bright matrix; κ-carbides preferentially precipitate at the edge of (Ti, V)C carbides while almost no κ-carbides precipitate in the matrix.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: TEM samples mechanically ground to 50 μm thickness, 3 mm diameter discs punched and ion-polished to electron transparency.
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the κ-carbides and (Ti, V)C carbides in M2 steel aged for 10 h (BF/DF imaging and SAED).
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) - bright-field (BF), dark-field/centred dark-field (DF/CDF) imaging and selected-area electron diffraction (SAED)

analytical_models.model_name: Olson–Cohen SFE model (with grain-size excess term)
analytical_models.model_note: Calculated SFE of M2 ≈ 78 mJ/m², indicating the deformation mode of the material is dislocation slip; Ti and V have little influence on the SFE.

parameters.name: ρ (molar surface density on {111} planes, M2)

computational_details.simulation_method: Olson–Cohen thermodynamic model for stacking-fault energy (SFE)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The calculated SFE (dislocation-slip regime) is consistent with TEM observation of planar slip deformation in M1 and M2 after tensile testing.

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: The non-shearable (Ti, V)C carbides cannot be cut by dislocations and hinder dislocation motion (Orowan bypassing); a region of higher dislocation density forms around them, increasing the flow stress.

interfaces.interface_notes: For the aged M2-30 material, the (002) plane of (Ti, V)C is parallel to the (001) plane of κ-carbide, i.e. (002)(Ti,V)C || (001)κ; this orientation relationship was determined for M2-30 (Fig. 6), not explicitly for M2-10.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Before aging, pre-existing (Ti, V)C carbides are distributed in the austenite matrix with surrounding carbon-enriched zones; upon aging at 550 °C, κ-carbides preferentially precipitate along the edge of the (Ti, V)C carbides using these carbon-rich regions as precipitation sites.

phase_interfaces.coherence: κ-carbide nucleates/precipitates heterogeneously at the edge of the (Ti, V)C carbide; intergrown

interfaces.slip_behavior: Planar dislocation slip; the calculated SFE of M2 (≈78 mJ/m²) indicates dislocation slip as the deformation mode, and TEM of the deformed region confirms planar slip for M2.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Material was melted in a high-vacuum electric-arc melting furnace (starting step for the M2 steel ingot).
Ingots hot rolled from 20 to 2 mm at 1000 °C followed by water quenching.
M2 after solution treatment is named M2-SS; solution treatment at 1000 °C for 30 min followed by water quenching.
Aging of M2 at 550 °C for 10 h followed by water quenching; this condition is named M2-10.

phases_present.morphology: nanoscale precipitates at the edge of (Ti, V)C carbides

precipitates.distribution: intragranular, dispersed within the austenite grain interior

precipitates.coherency: coherent with the austenite matrix (shearable by dislocations)
precipitates.distribution: heterogeneous; preferentially precipitates at the edge of (Ti, V)C carbides, with almost no κ-carbides precipitating in the matrix

structures.overall_structure: Single-phase austenite (γ) matrix containing intragranular (Ti, V)C carbides; after aging, κ-carbides heterogeneously precipitate at the edge of the (Ti, V)C carbides while almost no κ-carbides precipitate in the matrix.

unmapped_findings: The paper reports that aged M2 steel reached a yield strength of 884 MPa (with only a slight decrease in elongation) and that Ti/V addition increases the tensile strength from 1004 MPa to 1096 MPa; however, the tensile figure (Fig. 7) legend lists M2-30 (not M2-10), so this mechanical-property data could not be unambiguously assigned to the M2-10 (10 h aged) sample and is therefore not placed in this sample's properties.

Quantitative (Ti, V)C data for the 10 h aged M2 condition (M2-10) are not tabulated separately: the volume-fraction/mean-radius table reports only M1-SS, M1-30, M2-SS ((Ti, V)C 2.4 ± 1.4 %, 35.8 ± 20.1 nm) and M2-30 ((Ti, V)C 2.3 ± 1.7 %, 37.1 ± 22.6 nm); b0035 states the (Ti, V)C size/volume fraction do not change under aging.

κ-carbide volume fraction and mean radius for M2-10 are not reported separately; the tabulated κ values (3.2 ± 2.8 %, 9.7 ± 8.5 nm) belong to M2-30. Only the qualitative statement that in M2-10 the κ-carbides precipitate heterogeneously at the (Ti, V)C edges with almost no matrix κ-carbides is given.
Grain size of the M2-10 sample is not reported; Table 2 gives grain sizes only for M1-SS (42.4 ± 7.8 μm), M1-30 (45.3 ± 9.3 μm), M2-SS (32.3 ± 10.4 μm) and M2-30 (35.8 ± 12.7 μm).
